name: Grapple Wars 1: Fight For The Right

date.source: The league's status post of 14 June 1993 gives the event as "this Friday (18th)" and the script was posted on 18 June 1993.

evidence.note: Part one of the script: the first five matches and their backstage interviews.
Part two of the script: matches six to eleven and the show's closing copyright line.

matches.note: The Great Tadaka pinned the Gross Gladiator for the Master of the Ring title after referee Don Animal counted three over a shoulder the announcers thought was off the mat.
title: mbwf-1992-master-of-the-ring

matches.note: Angel Pit Bull beat the Countess with her Flip Side finisher for the Ladies World Championship.
title: mbwf-1992-ladies-world

matches.note: The Electric Youth rolled up Scourge to keep the Air Wave Championship.
title: mbwf-1992-air-wave

matches.note: Terror pinned Master 'Bud' Wiser, who made no effort to kick out, and Pain Unbound won the World Tag Team Championship.
title: mbwf-1992-tag-team

matches.note: Death Croc made Wolverine submit to the Croc Bite and won the World Championship.
title: mbwf-1992-world

name: Friday Ferocity: Show #1

date.source: The re-run post's own wording, "the results of the draw for the first 3 matches of 1993", and its next week's draw, Death Croc against Wolverine for the World title (promotions/mbwf-1992/archive/m-b-w-f-re-run-friday-ferocity-1-1995-06-12.html): the newsletter of 18 March 1993 puts that match at Friday Ferocity Show #2 on 26 February 1993 and the weekly Friday shows run on (#5 on 19 March, #6 on 26 March), so show #1 fell a week before, about 19 February 1993 (promotions/mbwf-1992/archive/m-b-w-f-news-1993-03-18.html).

no_appearances_reason: Only the Slammers' main-event win is credited here; the show's other entrants are not minted records.
